title: Cadence retrospective entry
description: Structured JSON form of a single retrospective finding, drafted by the Reviewer subagent and used as the basis for FRAMEWORK_CHANGELOG.md entries.

feature.description: Name of the feature run this retrospective covers

what_happened.description: One-line description of the observed issue

auto_catchable.description: Whether the issue could be caught mechanically

auto_method.description: If auto_catchable, what mechanism would catch it (lint, schema, AST check)

rule_reference.description: ADR-NNNN or PATTERNS.md §X if rule_existed was true

landed_in.description: Commit SHA, PR number, or other reference where the approved fix landed

near_miss.description: True if this is a gap that turned out fine, false if a real issue caught

factory.description: Present only on findings the factory's learning loop records (tool/signals.py; see docs/LEARNING.md). Holds ids, hashes and validated keys, never comment or code text. Manual /cadence-retro findings leave it out.

class_key.description: The mistake class, built by code as family:body. Identical strings are the same class.

trust.description: A: read statically from the patch or the GitHub API. B: parsed from output the agent can influence, checked against the base tree. C: a model's label, counted only where code verified it.

gate_caught.description: The Definition of Done gate blocked the attempt.

reached_pr.description: The attempt was published as a pull request.

rule_id.description: The boundary rule that fired, if any.

excerpt_sha256.description: sha256 of the comment body. The text itself is never stored.

judge.description: Hook for a later shadow judge (Jev or an LLM). Always null in v1.

violation_sample.description: Structured form of the offending code. Consumed by tool/emit_rule.py for Layer 3 boundary-class findings: lets the framework auto-generate a fixture + boundary rule and verify the rule actually fires on this exact sample before the finding is recorded as landed.

kind.description: Which auto-emitter handles this sample. Only 'boundary-rule' is wired in v0.3.0-rc.1; future emitters (lint-rule, schema-rule) will add enum values.

language.description: File extension hint for the generated fixture. The checker is language-agnostic, but the fixture file needs the right extension to be scanned.

where.description: Glob pattern for the file location that must not perform this import (matches cadence.yaml boundaries[].where). Example: 'src/features/**'. Letters, digits and _ . @ * - /; it may not start with '/'. tool/emit_rule.py also refuses '..' segments and a tests/fixtures/ prefix.

import_line.description: The exact offending import line as it appeared in the source: one line, at most 300 characters. The emitter writes this verbatim into the generated fixture.

forbidden_pattern.description: Glob the import resolves to that the rule must forbid (matches cadence.yaml boundaries[].forbidden[]). Example: 'src/data/sources/**'. Same character set as 'where'.

reason.description: Why this boundary exists. Becomes the cadence.yaml rule's reason field; surfaces in the checker's error output.
